phase3_findings.description: cmd_update_baseline calls scan() without a skipped accumulator, so a temporarily-unreadable file silently drops its pending row from the reseeded baseline. Downstream-neutralized: the next --check fails closed on the still-unreadable file and re-reports it once readable. Agent states this needs no change.

The transient exception (.changeset/README.md stays pending) is only implicitly asserted via the aggregate clean rc=0; an explicit --print-population assertion would name it directly. Clarity gap, not a behavioral hole.

A bucket record that is valid JSON but missing the top-level 'frozen' key exits via an uncaught KeyError rather than the fail-closed exit 2; only JSONDecodeError is covered. The tooling file is not adversarially mutable, so low priority.

report: Convergence re-review of PR #1973 (issue #1745) at head dc631e8. The shadow-caught Critical (false RED on main after version-consolidate deletes a consumed changeset) is GENUINELY RESOLVED: classify() checks transient_prefixes first in the first-match chain, returning ('transient', total, 0) so a .changeset/ file (minus transient_exceptions) is never added to pending and never baselined, removing it from both the forward guard and the reverse stale-row check. The self-referencing .changeset/issue-1745 baseline row was removed; cmd_update_baseline reseeds through the same transient-excluding scan(), so the record stays self-consistent. .changeset/README.md is carved back out and retains its pending baseline row (count 2). The regression is directly tested in run.sh: a transient changeset needs no baseline row, deleting a transient changeset (the merge-time behavior) does not fire a stale-row RED, and a malformed bucket record fails closed with exit 2. Real-tree lint runs clean: audited 1120 of 1120 files, rc=0. Docstring and JSON _comment claims verified true against shipped code (transient bucket behavior, and the corrected '--check -> the default (no flag)' wording — the old '--check (default)' was itself a documented falsehood since no --check flag exists in argparse). NO new at-or-above-Important issue introduced by the fix. Three non-blocking Suggestions remain (one explicitly marked needs-no-change, two optional robustness/clarity items). Prior known Suggestions (cosmetic audited N of N, repo_root cwd fallback, intentional git-ls-files fail-closed traceback) parked, not re-raised. Scope note: ships enforcement mechanism only; mass prose sweep (AC2) deferred to follow-up; in-scope AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6 met. Verdict: APPROVE.
